transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 09:21 AM -05:00
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Danielle Carter (Harborpoint Head of Cloud), Miguel Torres (CISO), Lisa Nguyen (PM), Ethan Brooks (Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Priya is our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing this morning?
[00:10] Danielle Carter: Good morning, thanks. We wanted to use this time to walk through our compliance needs and see how Redwood fits for both hosted and private options.
[00:20] Miguel Torres: Quick intro, I'm Miguel, CISO. We're focused on ensuring no customer data leaves our allowed regions, strict logging controls, and that we can produce audit trails for regulators.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. High level, we'll go over deployment modes — hosted, dedicated reserve, private/VPC — and how each handles data residency, logs, KMS, and audit capabilities. Feel free to interrupt me.
[00:45] Lisa Nguyen: We'll also flag our requirements up front: EU resident data must remain in EU datacenters, some HIPAA-bound flows, and retention windows that vary by data class.

[01:05] Priya Shah: Understood. For Hosted — we have region controls so requests can be routed to specific regions, but hosted customers typically rely on our SOC2 and contractual commitments. We offer EU-hosted endpoints and EU-only routing. However — hosted still means Redwood manages the control plane.
[01:30] Miguel Torres: That's one of our questions: managed control plane — does that mean metadata or logs could be replicated outside EU?
[01:38] Jordan Mills: Good question. For hosted EU-only customers, our control plane operations are scoped to EU regions. For contract-level guarantees we include data residency clauses and can provide SOC 2 and GDPR documentation.
[01:52] Ethan Brooks: On logging: we need to ensure that any logs that might contain PII are either not captured or redacted before leaving the environment. Does Redwood stream request/response logs back to your central logging?
[02:05] Priya Shah: By default we capture operational logs and error traces. Customers can opt out of storing full request payloads in Redwood logs. We also support configurable log redaction rules at ingestion and can integrate with customer-managed logging sinks via VPC peering or S3 endpoints for dedicated/private deployments.
[02:30] Danielle Carter: So for Hosted EU, if we enable redaction, are the raw tokens ever persisted in any US backups? We need guarantees for GDPR and local regulator audits.
[02:40] Priya Shah: For EU-only hosted, backups and replicas are kept within EU unless you agree otherwise. We can also arrange contractual terms for data localization and limit backups to EU buckets. We'll provide the DPA and a data flow diagram in the compliance pack.

[03:05] Miguel Torres: HIPAA — some of our flows are BAA-bound. Do you support HIPAA/BAA and can we get a Business Associate Agreement for hosted and private?
[03:15] Jordan Mills: Yes, we support HIPAA and sign BAAs for both dedicated and private deployments. For hosted, we do sign BAAs for customers that meet certain onboarding requirements; we can include that in the legal packet.
[03:26] Lisa Nguyen: For Dedicated — what changes operationally vs Hosted?
[03:30] Priya Shah: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and logical isolation. Importantly for compliance: you can restrict logs to your own storage, integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption, and choose network isolation via VPC peering. The control plane still handles orchestration but we can provide tighter SLAs and options for limiting telemetry that leaves your network.
[03:55] Danielle Carter: That control plane detail matters — if the control plane is outside our network, we need to evaluate what metadata it sees. Can we run a private control plane?
[04:05] Priya Shah: Yes, that's our Private deployment option — we offer a private control plane that can be run inside your VPC or on-prem. That decouples orchestration and audit logs from Redwood-managed infrastructure. Many regulated banks choose Private for that reason.

[04:30] Miguel Torres: KMS/HSM: we require customer-managed keys and hardware-backed keys for some data classes. How does Redwood integrate?
[04:38] Priya Shah: We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure KeyVault) and can support HSM-backed keys via those services. For Private deployments we can also support direct HSM integrations where keys never leave your HSM.
[04:55] Ethan Brooks: Do logs ever include decryption material or key identifiers that could help reconstruct plaintext?
[05:00] Priya Shah: No, we don't log private key material. We do log key IDs for operational reasons but customers can mask or redact those in Dedicated/Private setups.

[05:20] Jordan Mills: A common ask is whether request/response content is stored for debugging. We let customers toggle request retention. For regulated flows you typically turn it off and send sanitized or redacted payloads to us for debugging, or run a POC in Private where logs never leave your VPC.
[05:40] Danielle Carter: How about audit logs retention — regulators ask for 7 years in some cases. Can we export complete audit trails?
[05:48] Priya Shah: Yes, audit logs can be exported to your storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with configurable retention. For Hosted we can export logs to customer-managed buckets, and for Dedicated/Private it's standard to route logs to your retention stores.

[06:10] Miguel Torres: We have strict e-discovery and right-to-be-forgotten processes. If a user requests deletion, how do you handle purging from backups?
[06:20] Jordan Mills: We support deletion workflows and can provide certifications of deletion. For Hosted customers with EU-only contractual terms, backups are scoped to region but de-duplication windows can mean full immediate purge from backups is constrained by system snapshot policies; we document these in the DPA. Private gives you the most control for immediate purge.

[06:50] Lisa Nguyen: On the practical side, what's the path for a POC? We'd like to try a few endpoints with redacted traffic and run a couple of compliance checks and load tests.
[07:00] Priya Shah: Typical path: start with a Hosted EU-only trial with redaction and restricted telemetry, run functional tests. For higher assurance we then do a Dedicated reserved capacity POC with VPC peering and customer KMS. If you need complete control, we scope a Private on-prem/VPC pilot.
[07:20] Danielle Carter: Can Redwood sign EU DPA, BAA, and provide SOC 2 reports and ISO certs?
[07:28] Jordan Mills: Yes — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 certificates, GDPR DPA, and BAA are all in our compliance pack. I'll include the latest audit PDFs.

[07:45] Miguel Torres: Network-level controls — do you support VPC endpoints, private link, or peering rather than public internet?
[07:52] Priya Shah: Yes. Dedicated and Private support VPC peering, PrivateLink (or equivalent) and customer-managed NATs. Hosted can support private endpoints in some cloud regions via partner connectivity; we'll map the exact options in the tech deep dive.

[08:10] Ethan Brooks: One specific regulatory ask — logs must not contain more than a hashed reference to account numbers. Can Redwood help with redaction/hashing at ingest?
[08:20] Priya Shah: We have pre-ingest redaction rules and a redaction pipeline that can hash or remove patterns. For high-assurance you can perform redaction client-side before sending.

[08:40] Lisa Nguyen: Cost/tradeoff question — is Dedicated significantly more expensive than Hosted? We're trying to build out cost models.
[08:48] Jordan Mills: Dedicated has higher baseline cost because of reserved capacity, but it reduces per-token variability and gives you predictable latency and isolation. Private has additional engineering/setup fees. We'll send a pricing comparison for your expected qps and token volumes.

[09:05] Priya Shah: Also to call out technical capabilities: our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce token cost; in some transcripts and older docs that term becomes 'K V cash' in notes, sorry, transcription quirk — but operationally it's KV cache. For Private deployments we can tune caching behavior to avoid persisting sensitive prefixes.

[09:30] Miguel Torres: About telemetry: can we disable crash traces and full stack traces that might include PII?
[09:36] Priya Shah: Yes, telemetry level is configurable. For Dedicated/Private we can set telemetry to minimal and disable stack traces. Hosted customers can request reduced telemetry but will need contractual terms for full suppression.

[09:55] Jordan Mills: Any other blockers or must-haves from your side?
[10:00] Danielle Carter: We need a written statement on data residency and backup locality, an example DPA that states EU-only processing, and sample config docs for VPC peering and KMS setup.
[10:10] Miguel Torres: Also need confirmation that we can produce audit-ready logs with immutable timestamps for compliance audits and forensics.
[10:18] Priya Shah: That's supported. We can export signed audit logs and support write-once buckets for long-term retention.

[10:35] Lisa Nguyen: Who at Redwood will be our technical point of contact during POC?
[10:40] Jordan Mills: Priya will be the SE lead; I'll be the commercial owner. We'll introduce an engineer from the deployment team if we scope Private or Dedicated.

[10:52] Priya Shah: Next steps recap — Jordan will send compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, DPA, BAA boilerplate), Priya will propose two time slots for technical deep dive and POC scoping, Harborpoint will share redacted traffic profile and retention policy, Miguel will share list of internal auditors.
[11:10] Danielle Carter: Sounds good. We may want to schedule the deep dive mid-next week — our windows are Tue/Wed afternoons.
[11:20] Jordan Mills: I'll propose Wed 3/11 and Thu 3/12; Priya, does that work?
[11:25] Priya Shah: Works for me, I'll send calendar invites.

[11:35] Miguel Torres: A last thing — competitors: we're also talking to Anthropic and evaluating an internal self-hosted path. Anthropic's EU coverage is good, but we prefer a vendor that supports private control plane for auditability.
[11:50] Jordan Mills: Great to know. We'll make sure to address those differentiators in the follow-up.

[12:00] Lisa Nguyen: Thanks everyone.
[12:03] Jordan Mills: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[12:07] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K V cash' instead of KV cache, some names slightly off). This export preserves speaker labels and timestamps but may have minor mis-attributions.
